page_placements.theme: Measurement of refusal and bypass depends on scorer, decoding and serving setup

record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file list only; the linked WRITEUP.md and code were not provided or read. The README reports results, but the code was not run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports experiments on whether LLM judges label refusal-shaped transcripts as compliant. It does not test or rely on the claimed residual-stream direction, its ablation, or any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern judges' labels for transcripts, not whether the judge models themselves refuse harmful requests or whether a direction mediates refusal. Recorded as findings on a related but different construct; no claim-version verdicts apply.
record.test_reason: The repo studies whether open-weight LLM judges mislabel refusal transcripts as COMPLIANT. Its 'ablation' means editing transcripts in matched pairs, not removing a residual-stream direction. No refusal direction is computed, ablated, added, or mentioned. No model's own refusal rate is measured, so no claim version is tested. Strictly, the repo neither cites nor discusses the refusal-direction work; 'discusses' is the closest available relation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README concludes that open-weight judges (7B–14B) conflate partial compliance with compliance, causally in all four judges, while cooperative tone has a small effect mainly in hermes3:8b. Two points should be added. First, the original question, consequence-framing 'motivated mislabeling', is faint at this scale: deltas are at most about 8% with overlapping intervals. Second, the 14B judge was less accurate than the 8B ones, so the authors argue the failure is not a low-capacity artifact.
record.recipe_differences: This is an evaluation repo about LLM-judge reliability on refusal-shaped transcripts, not a replication or implementation of the residual-stream refusal-direction method.
record.method_sensitivity: Judge model and transcript condition affect the reported mislabel rates; the README also reports consequence-framing and rubric conditions, but these do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: On the 28-transcript corpus, every judge mislabels procedural/mundane control refusals more often than value-loaded refusals. Separation runs from -5.2% (llama3.1:8b) to -48.3% (qwen2.5:14b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM judges misclassify process-grounded refusals as compliance more than value-grounded ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Executing a partial action before refusing raised judge mislabel rates by 14.8 to 30.5 points in all four judges (p≤0.0025, 8 matched pairs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial compliance causes LLM judges to label refusals as compliant.

fits_no_version.finding: Deleting only the cooperative-gesture clause changed mislabel rates little. The effect was +8.3 for hermes3:8b, +4.2 (sub-threshold) for qwen2.5:14b, and null for mistral and llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cooperative tone alone weakly and judge-dependently biases LLM judges toward COMPLIANT.

record.problems: Evidence is reported in the README, while the underlying write-up and code were not read or run. The README notes that the consequence-framing effect is faint at this scale, that some comparisons have overlapping Wilson intervals, and that the sample is too small for per-family claims.
record.rows_left_out: The README's consequence-framing grids and pooled tables were not extracted because they concern the judge's consequence-sensitive labeling rather than the target residual-stream refusal-direction claim; no rows were omitted for a tested version.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction; no ablation or addition; no refusal rate or capability measure.
No weight edit or abliteration of released models.
No jailbreaks and no analysis of direction suppression; no adversarial training.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis.
No internal representation of harmfulness versus refusal.
No transfer across languages, variants or base/instruct models.
No reasoning-model mechanistic analysis. 'Reasoned' here is a judge prompt format, not a test of a direction.

record.verdict_notes: Off-topic for refusal_direction. The repo shares only the word 'ablation' (transcript edits) and 'refusal' (refusal-shaped transcripts being judged). Only the README was available; WRITEUP.md and the preprint were not read. Consequence-framing grids were rightly left out as irrelevant to every version.

versions.untested_parts: No residual-stream direction is measured, ablated or added; refusal behavior and other capabilities are not tested.
No weight edit or removal of refusal behavior in released models.
No attack suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No encoding of harmfulness judgments or refusal decisions is measured.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
No refusal training procedure or training stage is tested.
No reasoning models are tested for the claimed direction.

relation.reason: The text never mentions, cites or discusses the refusal direction, Arditi et al., or abliteration. The only 'direction' in it refers to the sign of the consequence-framing delta.

tranche.reason: The study is about how reliably LLM judges label refusal transcripts. Its 'ablation' means minimal edits to transcripts. It never computes or uses a residual-stream refusal direction.

source_check.notes: Off-topic for refusal_direction. It was probably retrieved because the words 'ablation' and 'refusal' match. The judges are Ollama Q4_K_M quantized models. The text holds only the README and a file list (WRITEUP.md and the preprint are not included), but every row comes from the README.

statements.correction: 28-transcript corpus, reasoned/default, standard+reversed pooled; separation = control mean (procedural + mundane) minus value-loaded mean; negative in all four judges, from -5.2% (llama3.1:8b) to -48.3% (qwen2.5:14b). Partial-action matched pairs (8 pairs): effect +14.8 (mistral:7b) to +30.5 points (hermes3:8b), all four judges, p<=0.0025.
statements.problem: Separation compares the pooled control mean (procedural AND mundane) with the value-loaded mean, not procedural refusals alone. All the numbers are correct.
